claim: The Alessi factory outlet sits at via privata Alessi 6 in Crusinallo di Omegna, open Mon–Sun 10:00–18:00, selling catalogue items plus discounted seconds and end-of-range pieces next to the Alessi factory itself.
quote: The Alessi outlet store is located at 6 privata Alessi street in Crusinallo di Omegna, and is open Monday to Sunday from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

claim: The Museo Alessi, across the driveway from the outlet, requires booking at least two weeks ahead for a guided visit with a team member.
quote: The Museo Alessi is across the driveway from the outlet store, and reservations are required at least two weeks in advance to see the museum with a member of the team.

claim: Forum Omegna occupies the reconverted Cobianchi steelworks site and was designed by Alessandro Mendini, hosting since 1998 a permanent collection of household design from Alessi, Calderoni, Girmi, Lagostina, La Nuova Faro, Irmel, Tracanzan and Piazza.
quote: The reconversion of the area from a place of work and hardship to a new cultural and artistic center was entrusted to the prestigious studio of the architect Mendini... Since 1998, the Forum in Omegna has housed a rich collection of household objects by companies that have made Italian and world history

claim: The Sanctuary of Madonna del Sasso rises on a granite outcrop above Pella at 338 m, completed in 1748 with a Greek-cross Baroque plan, frescoes by Lorenzo Peracino and an altarpiece Pietà by Fermo Stella da Caravaggio.
quote: stands on a granite rock rising above the village of Pella and the mirror of Lake Orta at an altitude of 338 meters... The church has a Greek cross plan in Baroque style... the architecture and frescoes are the work of the Valsesian painter-architect Lorenzo Peracino.

claim: The forecourt of the sanctuary is locally called the 'balcony of Cusio' and offers a panorama spanning the lake, Mottarone, the Alps and the Novara plain.
quote: From the square in front of the church, called "the balcony of Cusio", there is a breathtaking view of almost the entire lake, Mount Mottarone, the Alps, and the plain towards Novara.

claim: San Maurizio d'Opaglio's Museo del Rubinetto e della sua Tecnologia is billed as unique in the world, telling the story of human relationships with water through faucet and valve technology.
quote: Museum of the Faucet and its Technology of San Maurizio d'Opaglio is unique in the world; it addresses the fascinating relationship of humans with water through the history of hygiene and technological innovations

claim: San Maurizio d'Opaglio is known as the 'capital of the faucet'; the museum offers free admission Friday–Sunday 15:00–18:00.
quote: San Maurizio d'Opaglio is known as the "capital of the faucet"... Admission is free, and hours are Friday-Sunday from 3:00 pm to 6:00 pm.

claim: Pettenasco's Museo dell'Arte della Tornitura del Legno occupies a former Maulini family wood-turning workshop that operated 1886–1970, sited in the historic centre near the Medieval House and town hall square.
quote: the museum is located in an old wood turning workshop that belongs to the Maulini family, which operated their business there from 1886 to 1970. The museum is situated in the historic center of Pettenasco a few steps from the Medieval House and Town Hall Square.

claim: Wood turning was the defining Cusio craft, with many workshops producing turned-wood objects in the area until the 1950s, when industrial homeware took over.
quote: Wood turning was a typical type of craftsmanship in the Cusio area, with many businesses producing objects in turned wood until the Fifties.

claim: Cantine Aperte Alto Piemonte 2026 runs 30–31 May with Gattinara DOCG, Ghemme DOCG, Boca, Bramaterra and Colline Novaresi cellars open for visits.
quote: Cantine Aperte Alto Piemonte 2026 will be held on May 30 and 31, with Gattinara DOCG, Ghemme DOCG, Boca, Bramaterra and Colline Novaresi opening their doors.

claim: The Strada del Vino delle Colline Novaresi spans 13 municipalities including Boca, Ghemme, Sizzano, Fara Novarese, Romagnano Sesia, Briona, Suno and Cavaglio d'Agogna.
quote: The Wine Route of the Novarese Hills involves 13 municipalities including Barengo, Boca, Bogogno, Briona, Cavaglio d'Agogna, Cressa, Fara Novarese, Ghemme, Marano Ticino, Mezzomerico, Romagnano Sesia, Sizzano and Suno.

claim: Villa Crespi confirms that Ghemme and Gattinara cellars are about 30 minutes from Lake Orta and offers a wine-tour package with private transfer.
quote: the wine cellars between Ghemme and Gattinara are just 30 minutes away from Lake Orta, and Villa Crespi offers organized wine tours to this area with private transfer.

claim: Tapulone is the culinary symbol of Borgomanero — a slow-cooked stew of minced donkey meat with lard, onion, garlic, red wine, cabbage, bay, cloves and rosemary, served with polenta.
quote: Tapulone is a traditional dish and a culinary symbol of the city of Borgomanero... It's prepared with beaten lard, extra virgin olive oil, onions, garlic, local red wine, minced donkey meat, cabbage, and various herbs and spices such as bay leaves, cloves, and rosemary.

claim: Monte Mottarone sits between Lake Orta and Lake Maggiore and is accessible by road from Armeno on the Lake Orta side via provincial road 41, with the Stresa cableway closed since the May 2021 disaster.
quote: One road to the peak comes up from Armeno, west of the Mottarone summit near Lake Orta... It is possible to reach the top by car from Lake Orta and Armeno through the provincial road 41.

claim: Alfonso Bialetti, born 1888 in Omegna, opened an aluminium semi-finished products workshop there in 1919 and invented the Moka Express in 1933; the 'omino con i baffi' logo was added in 1953 and a state-of-the-art Omegna factory followed in 1956.
quote: Alfonso Bialetti was born in 1888 in Omegna, in the northern Italian region of Piedmont. In 1919 in the village of Omegna, Piedmonte, Alfonso Bialetti opened a workshop for the manufacture of aluminum semi-finished products.

claim: Omegna's homeware lineage — Lagostina, Alessi, Piazza, Bialetti — grew out of the Cane family's pioneering metalworking; Lagostina's 1955 'Thermoplan' double-bottom innovation paired steel and aluminium.
quote: It was Lagostina who once again found a solution in 1955 by using bases made of "Thermoplan"®: a system that involved coupling steel and aluminium in order to create the so-called "double bottom".

claim: Miacce are paper-thin waffle-like discs made since the 15th century in a long-handled iron heated over fire, batter of milk, flour and eggs, served with soft cheese or jam — round in Piedmont, rectangular in Valle d'Aosta.
quote: Miacce are crispy paper-thin treats made since the 15th century in a waffle iron called a notai heated over an open fire, prepared from a batter of milk, flour (wheat or corn) and eggs, and often served with soft cheeses or jam.

claim: Gorgonzola DOP can legally be produced only in a defined set of provinces including Novara and Verbano-Cusio-Ossola, putting the cheese's heartland directly around Lake Orta.
quote: Gorgonzola can only be produced in the provinces of Novara, Bergamo, Brescia, Como, Cremona, Cuneo, Lecco, Lodi, Milan, Pavia, Varese, Verbano-Cusio-Ossola and Vercelli
